name: Caointeach

attributes.attribute: a Highland name for the banshee
a spirit that wailed by a waterfall
wept loudly before a great disaster
mourned for days before the Glencoe massacre
washed the clothes of the doomed at night
was kind and wept with human grief
a spirit that washed clothes to warn of death

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text: Caointeach is a spirit of the Scottish Highlands. Highlanders use the name Caoineag for her as well. Wailer and weeper are the senses of the two words. She belongs to the family of the banshee. Her cry alerted people that a death drew near. Before any demise she would sit near a waterfall and weep, but for a great calamity she raised a far louder cry. The Caointeach belonging to the Macdonalds spent days in mourning ahead of the terrible massacre at Glencoe. On some nights she washed the clothes of those fated to die, just as the Washer at the Ford did. She held no malice toward anyone. Human sorrow moved her and made her weep even harder. Yet folk chose to ignore her. The rule was to refuse her any reward, because a gift would make her vanish and leave the family without warning of a death. The Welsh form of this being carries its own name, the Cyhyreath, whose voice mimics the sighs and groans of dying people.

okr.objective: Caointeach is a Highland spirit whose cry tells of a death to come.
key_results: Caointeach is the Highland name for the banshee, that is the wailer.
